title: usrloc Module
content_markdown: A SIP user location implementation. Its main purpose is to store, manage and provide access to SIP registration bindings (contacts) for other modules (e.g. registrar, mid-registrar, nathelper, etc.). The module exports no functions that could be directly used from the OpenSIPS script. At runtime, the contacts may reside in memory, in an SQL database or in a NoSQL database. Combinations of two of the above are also possible. For example, contacts may only be directly manipulated in memory in order to guarantee fast interactions while being asynchronously synchronized to an SQL database. The latter helps achieve restart persistency. Consult the working_mode_preset parameter for more details on all possible runtime behaviors of the module. The OpenSIPS user location implementation is cluster-enabled. On top of supporting traditional "single instance" setups, it also allows multiple OpenSIPS user location nodes to form a single, global user location cluster. This allows high-level features such as startup synchronization (data tunneling) from a random, healthy "donor" node and evenly distributed NAT pinging workloads.
overview: A SIP user location implementation. Its main purpose is to store, manage and provide access to SIP registration bindings (contacts) for other modules (e.g. registrar, mid-registrar, nathelper, etc.). The module exports no functions that could be directly used from the OpenSIPS script. At runtime, the contacts may reside in memory, in an SQL database or in a NoSQL database. Combinations of two of the above are also possible. For example, contacts may only be directly manipulated in memory in order to guarantee fast interactions while being asynchronously synchronized to an SQL database. The latter helps achieve restart persistency. Consult the working_mode_preset parameter for more details on all possible runtime behaviors of the module. The OpenSIPS user location implementation is cluster-enabled. On top of supporting traditional "single instance" setups, it also allows multiple OpenSIPS user location nodes to form a single, global user location cluster. This allows high-level features such as startup synchronization (data tunneling) from a random, healthy "donor" node and evenly distributed NAT pinging workloads.
how_it_works: Starting with OpenSIPS 2.4, the user location module offers several optional data distribution models, each tailoring to specific real-life production use cases. Built on top of the OpenSIPS clustering module, these models take into account service concerns such as high availability, geographical distribution, horizontal scalability and NAT traversal. Depending on data locality, the distribution models are split in two main categories: "Federation" Topology and "Full Sharing" Topology. The federation topology keeps contact data local to the original OpenSIPS node, publishing light "metadata" to share reachability. The full sharing topology broadcasts contact information to all data nodes. The module also solves the "N Contact Pings" Problem by using the cluster layer to partition and spread the pinging workload evenly across nodes. Contact matching (for the same Address-of-Record, AoR) is handled via algorithms including "Contact based only" (strict RFC 3261 compliancy) and "Contact and Call-ID based" (an extension for NAT traversal contexts).

exported_parameters.name: use_domain
exported_parameters.description: If the domain part of the user should be also saved and used for identifing the user (along with the username part). Useful in multi domain scenarios. Non 0 value means true.

exported_parameters.name: desc_time_order
exported_parameters.description: If the user's contacts should be kept timestamp ordered; otherwise the contact will be ordered based on q value. Non 0 value means true.

exported_parameters.name: timer_interval
exported_parameters.description:
Number of seconds between two timer runs. During each run, the module will update/delete dirty/expired contacts from memory and/or mirror these operations to the database, if configured to do so.

In case of an OpenSIPS shutdown or even a crash, contacts which are in memory only and have not been flushed yet to disk will NOT get lost! OpenSIPS will try its best to do a last-minute sync to DB right before shutting down.

exported_parameters.name: db_url
exported_parameters.description: URL of the database that should be used.

exported_parameters.name: cachedb_url
exported_parameters.description: URL of a NoSQL database to be used. Only required in a cachedb-enabled cluster_mode.

exported_parameters.name: db_mode
exported_parameters.description: This parameter has been kept for backwards compatibility. It acts as a working_mode_preset (which it also conflicts with), overriding any cluster_mode, restart_persistency and sql_write_mode settings.

exported_parameters.name: working_mode_preset
exported_parameters.description:
A pre-defined working mode for the usrloc module. Setting this parameter will override any cluster_mode, restart_persistency and sql_write_mode settings.

*   "single-instance-no-db" - This disables database completely. Only memory will be used. Contacts will not survive restart. Use this value if you need a really fast usrloc and contact persistence is not necessary or is provided by other means.
    
*   "single-instance-sql-write-through" - Write-Through scheme. All changes to usrloc are immediately reflected in database too. This is very slow, but very reliable. Use this scheme if speed is not your priority but need to make sure that no registered contacts will be lost during crash or reboot.
    
*   "single-instance-sql-write-back" - Write-Back scheme. This is a combination of previous two schemes. All changes are made to memory and database synchronization is done in the timer. The timer deletes all expired contacts and flushes all modified or new contacts to database. Use this scheme if you encounter high-load peaks and want them to process as fast as possible. The mode will not help at all if the load is high all the time. The added latency on the SIP signaling when using this asynchronous preset is much lower than the one added by the safe but blocking, "single-instance-sql-write-through" preset.
    
*   "sql-only" - DB-Only scheme. No memory cache is kept, all operations being directly performed with the database. The timer deletes all expired contacts from database - cleans after clients that didn't un-register or re-register. The mode is useful if you configure more servers sharing the same DB without any replication at SIP level. The mode may be slower due the high number of DB operation. For example NAT pinging is a killer since during each ping cycle all nated contact are loaded from the DB; The lack of memory caching also disable the statistics exports.
    
*   "federation-cachedb-cluster" - OpenSIPS will run with a "federation-cachedb" cluster_mode and "sync-from-cluster" restart_persistency. This will require the configuration of multiple "seed" nodes in the cluster. Refer to the _federated user location tutorial_ for more details.
    
*   "full-sharing-cluster" - OpenSIPS will run with a "full-sharing" cluster_mode and "sync-from-cluster" restart_persistency. This will require the configuration of one of the nodes in the cluster as a "seed" node in order to bootstrap the syncing process.
    
*   "full-sharing-cachedb-cluster" - OpenSIPS will run with a "full-sharing-cachedb" cluster_mode, where all location data strictly resides in a NoSQL database, thus it will have natural restart persistency.
    
Refer to section Distributed SIP User Location for details regarding the clustering topologies and their behavior.

exported_parameters.name: cluster_mode
exported_parameters.description:
This parameter will get overridden if either working_mode_preset or db_mode is set.

The behavior of the global OpenSIPS user location cluster. Refer to section Distributed SIP User Location for details.

This parameter may take the following values:

*   _"none"_ - single instance mode.
    
*   _"federation-cachedb"_ - federation-based data sharing. Local AoR metadata is published inside a NoSQL database, so other cluster nodes can fork SIP traffic over to the current node. Consequently, the location_cluster and cachedb_url parameters are mandatory.
    
*   _"full-sharing"_ - Broadcast contact updates (full-mesh mirroring) to all other OpenSIPS cluster participants. Each node will hold the entire user location dataset. Consequently, the location_cluster parameter is mandatory.
    
*   _"full-sharing-cachedb"_ - Full contact data management through the use of a NoSQL database (somewhat resembling the "sql-only" preset). The cluster layer is still required in order to be able to partition and spread the pinging workload evenly among participating OpenSIPS nodes. Consequently, the location_cluster and cachedb_url parameters are mandatory.
    
*   _"sql-only"_ - Multiple OpenSIPS boxes using a common db_url without necessarily being aware of each other.

exported_parameters.name: restart_persistency
exported_parameters.description:
This parameter will get overridden if either working_mode_preset or db_mode are set.

Controls the behavior of the OpenSIPS user location following a restart. This parameter has no effect in some database-only working mode presets, where restart persistency is naturally ensured.

This parameter may take the following values:

*   _"none"_ - no explicit data synchronization following a restart. The node starts empty.
    
*   _"load-from-sql"_ - enable SQL-based restart persistency. This causes all runtime in-memory writes (i.e. new registrations, re-registrations or de-registrations) to also propagate to an SQL database, from which all data will be imported following a restart. Choosing this value will make the db_url parameter mandatory, as well as cause sql_write_mode to default to "write-back" instead of "none".
    
*   _"sync-from-cluster"_ - enable cluster-based restart persistency. Following a restart, an OpenSIPS cluster node will search for a healthy "donor" node from which to mirror the entire user location dataset via direct cluster sync (TCP-based, binary-encoded data transfer). Depending on the clustering mode and cluster topology, this will require the configuration of one or multiple "seed" nodes in the cluster. Choosing this value will make the location_cluster parameter mandatory.

exported_parameters.name: sql_write_mode
exported_parameters.description:
This parameter will get overridden if either working_mode_preset or db_mode is set.

Only valid if restart_persistency is enabled. Controls the runtime behavior of OpenSIPS writes to the SQL database.

This parameter may take the following values:

*   _"none"_ - do not perform any additional SQL writes at runtime to an SQL database in order to specifically ensure restart persistency.
    
*   _"write-through"_ - all in-memory writes (i.e. new registrations, re-registrations or de-registrations) also propagate into the SQL database, inline. While this will definitely slow down registration performance (lookups are served from memory!), it has the advantage of making the instance crash-safe.
    
*   _"write-back"_ - all in-memory writes (i.e. new registrations, re-registrations or de-registrations) eventually also propagate into the SQL database, thanks to a separate timer routine. This dramatically speeds up registrations, but also introduces the possibility of crashing before the latest contact changes are propagated to the database. See the timer_interval for additional configuration.

exported_parameters.name: matching_mode
exported_parameters.description:
What contact matching algorithm to be used. Refer to section Contact Matching for the description of the algorithms.

The parameter may take the following values:

*   _0_ - CONTACT ONLY based matching algorithm.
    
*   _1_ - CONTACT and CALLID based matching algorithm.

exported_parameters.name: cseq_delay
exported_parameters.description:
Delay (in seconds) for accepting as retransmissions register requests with same Call-ID and Cseq. The delay is calculated starting from the receiving time of the first register with that Call-ID and Cseq.
Retransmissions within this delay interval will be accepted and replied as the original request, but no update will be done in location. If the delay is exceeded, error is reported.
A value of 0 disable the retransmission detection.

exported_parameters.name: location_cluster
exported_parameters.description:
Specifies the cluster ID which this instance will send to and receive from all user-location related information (addresses-of-record, contacts), organized into specific events (inserts, deletes or updates).
This OpenSIPS cluster exposes the "usrloc-contact-repl" capability in order to mark nodes as eligible for becoming data donors during an arbitrary sync request. Consequently, the cluster must have _at least one node_ marked with the "seed" value as the _clusterer.flags_ column/property in order to be fully functional. Consult the [clusterer - Capabilities](clusterer#capabilities) chapter for more details.
Default value is 0 (replication disabled).
More details on the user location distribution mechanisms are available under [Distributed SIP User Location](#distributed-sip-user-location "1.2.�Distributed SIP User Location").

exported_parameters.name: skip_replicated_db_ops
exported_parameters.default_value: 0 (upon receival of usrloc-related Binary Interface events, DB queries may be freely performed)
exported_parameters.description: Prevent OpenSIPS from performing any DB-related contact operations when events are received over the _Binary Interface_. This is commonly used to prevent unneeded duplicate operations.

exported_parameters.name: max_contact_delete
exported_parameters.description: Relevant only in WRITE_THROUGH or WRITE_BACK schemes. The maximum number of contacts to be deleted from the database at once. Will delete all of them, if fewer after passing through all the contacts.

exported_parameters.name: hash_size
exported_parameters.description: The number of entries of the hash table used by usrloc to store the location records is 2^hash_size. For hash_size=4, the number of entries of the hash table is 16. Since version 2.2, the maximu size of this parameter is 16, meaning that the hash supports maximum 65536 entries.

exported_parameters.name: regen_broken_contactid
exported_parameters.description: Since version 2.2, contact_id concept was introduced. Since this parameter validates a contact each time OpenSIPS is started, there are times when the value of this parameter should be regenerated. That is when location table is being migrated from a version older than 2.2 or when hash_size module parameter is changed. Enabling this parameter will regenerate broken contact id's based on current configurations.

exported_parameters.name: latency_event_min_us
exported_parameters.description: Defines a minimal pinging latency threshold, in microseconds, past which contact pinging latency update events will get raised. By default, an event is raised for each ping reply (i.e. latency update). If both latency_event_min_us and latency_event_min_us_delta are set, the event will get raised if either of them is true.

exported_parameters.name: latency_event_min_us_delta
exported_parameters.description: Defines a minimal, absolute pinging latency difference, in microseconds, past which contact pinging latency update events will get raised. The difference is computed using the latencies of the last two contact pinging replies. By default, an event is raised for each ping reply (i.e. latency update). If both latency_event_min_us and latency_event_min_us_delta are set, the event will get raised if either of them is true.

exported_parameters.name: pinging_mode
exported_parameters.description: Depending on the cluster_mode, the module can perform contact pinging using one of two possible heuristics: "ownership" - this instance will only attempt to ping a contact if it decides it is the logical owner of the contact. If a shared tag is attached to a contact, a node will keep sending pings to that contact as long as it owns the respective tag. If no shared tag has been specified for a given contact, the default is to assume permanent ownership of the contact and ping it upon request. "cooperation" - the assumption behind this pinging heuristic is that all user location cluster nodes are symmetrical (possibly front-ended by a SIP traffic balancing entity), such that either of them can ping any contact. Under this assumption, all currently online user location cluster nodes will cooperate and evenly split the pinging workload between them by hashing AoRs modulo current_number_of_online_nodes, and only picking the ones that they are responsible for. Notice that only the "full-sharing" clustering mode allows some flexibility -- all other modes are logically tied to a single pinging logic. Any unaccepted value, according to the above table, set for those modes will be silently discarded.
exported_parameters.notes: Any unaccepted value, according to the above table, set for those modes will be silently discarded.

exported_mi_functions.description: Empty the location table, then synchronize it with all contacts from memory. Note that this can not be used when no database is specified or with the DB-Only scheme. Important: make sure that all your contacts are in memory (_ul_dump_ MI function) before executing this command.

exported_mi_functions.name: ul_cluster_sync
exported_mi_functions.description: This command will only take effect if the target OpenSIPS instance is paired with a hot backup instance, while running under a cluster-enabled working_mode_preset. The current node will locate a healthy donor node within the location_cluster and issue a sync request to it. The donor node will then proceed to push all of its user location data over to the current node, via the binary interface. The received data will be merged with existing data. Conflicting contacts (matched according to matching_mode) are overwritten only if the sync data is newer than the current data.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.1. Set nat_bflag parameter
configuration_examples.description: The name of the branch flag to be used as NAT marker (if the contact is or not natted). This is a branch flag and it will be imported and used by all other modules depending on the usrloc module.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.2. Set contact_id_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of the column holding the unique contact IDs.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.3. Set user_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing usernames.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.4. Set user_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing domains.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.5. Set contact_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing contacts.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.6. Set expires_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing expires value.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.7. Set q_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing q values.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.8. Set callid_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing callid values.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.9. Set cseq_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing cseq numbers.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.10. Set methods_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing supported methods.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.11. Set flags_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column to save the internal flags of the record.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.12. Set cflags_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column to save the branch/contact flags of the record.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.13. Set user_agent_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing user-agent values.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.14. Set received_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing the source IP, port, and protocol from the REGISTER message.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.15. Set socket_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing the received socket information (IP:port) for the REGISTER message.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.16. Set path_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing the Path header.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.17. Set sip_instance_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing the SIP instance.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.18. Set kv_store_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing generic key-value data.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.19. Set attr_column parameter
configuration_examples.description: Name of column containing additional registration-related information.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.20. Set use_domain parameter
configuration_examples.description: If the domain part of the user should be also saved and used for identifing the user (along with the username part). Useful in multi domain scenarios. Non 0 value means true.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.21. Set desc_time_order parameter
configuration_examples.description: If the user's contacts should be kept timestamp ordered; otherwise the contact will be ordered based on q value. Non 0 value means true.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.22. Set timer_interval parameter
configuration_examples.description: Number of seconds between two timer runs. During each run, the module will update/delete dirty/expired contacts from memory and/or mirror these operations to the database, if configured to do so.
configuration_examples.explanation: In case of an OpenSIPS shutdown or even a crash, contacts which are in memory only and have not been flushed yet to disk will NOT get lost! OpenSIPS will try its best to do a last-minute sync to DB right before shutting down.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.23. Set db_url parameter
configuration_examples.description: URL of the database that should be used.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.24. Set cachedb_url parameter
configuration_examples.description: URL of a NoSQL database to be used. Only required in a cachedb-enabled cluster_mode.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.25. Set db_mode parameter
configuration_examples.description: This parameter has been kept for backwards compatibility. It acts as a working_mode_preset (which it also conflicts with), overriding any cluster_mode, restart_persistency and sql_write_mode settings.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.26. Set working_mode_preset parameter
configuration_examples.description: A pre-defined working mode for the usrloc module. Setting this parameter will override any cluster_mode, restart_persistency and sql_write_mode settings.
configuration_examples.explanation: Refer to section Distributed SIP User Location for details regarding the clustering topologies and their behavior.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.27. Set cluster_mode parameter
configuration_examples.description: The behavior of the global OpenSIPS user location cluster. Refer to section Distributed SIP User Location for details.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.28. Set restart_persistency parameter
configuration_examples.description: Controls the behavior of the OpenSIPS user location following a restart. This parameter has no effect in some database-only working mode presets, where restart persistency is naturally ensured.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.29. Set sql_write_mode parameter
configuration_examples.description: Only valid if restart_persistency is enabled. Controls the runtime behavior of OpenSIPS writes to the SQL database.
configuration_examples.explanation: Default value is "none" (no added SQL writes).

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.30. Set matching_mode parameter
configuration_examples.description: What contact matching algorithm to be used. Refer to section Contact Matching for the description of the algorithms.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.31. Set cseq_delay parameter
configuration_examples.description: Delay (in seconds) for accepting as retransmissions register requests with same Call-ID and Cseq. The delay is calculated starting from the receiving time of the first register with that Call-ID and Cseq.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.32. Setting the location_cluster parameter
configuration_examples.description: Specifies the cluster ID which this instance will send to and receive from all user-location related information (addresses-of-record, contacts), organized into specific events (inserts, deletes or updates).
configuration_examples.explanation: More details on the user location distribution mechanisms are available under Distributed SIP User Location.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.33. Setting the ha_cluster parameter
configuration_examples.description: Only relevant in "federation-cachedb" cluster_mode. Denotes the HA cluster ID to use in order to establish the active node within the HA pair, such that only that node performs WRITE operations to CacheDB.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.34. Setting the ha_shtag parameter
configuration_examples.description: Only relevant in "federation-cachedb" cluster_mode. Denotes the HA cluster sharing tag to use in order to establish the active node within the HA pair, such that only that node performs WRITE operations to CacheDB.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.35. Setting the skip_replicated_db_ops parameter
configuration_examples.description: Prevent OpenSIPS from performing any DB-related contact operations when events are received over the Binary Interface. This is commonly used to prevent unneeded duplicate operations.
configuration_examples.explanation: More details on the user location replication mechanism are available in Distributed SIP User Location

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.36. Setting the max_contact_delete parameter
configuration_examples.description: Relevant only in WRITE_THROUGH or WRITE_BACK schemes. The maximum number of contacts to be deleted from the database at once. Will delete all of them, if fewer after passing through all the contacts.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.37. Set hash_size parameter
configuration_examples.description: The number of entries of the hash table used by usrloc to store the location records is 2^hash_size. For hash_size=4, the number of entries of the hash table is 16. Since version 2.2, the maximu size of this parameter is 16, meaning that the hash supports maximum 65536 entries.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.38. Set regen_broken_contactid parameter
configuration_examples.description: Since version 2.2, contact_id concept was introduced. Since this parameter validates a contact each time OpenSIPS is started, there are times when the value of this parameter should be regenerated. That is when location table is being migrated from a version older than 2.2 or when hash_size module parameter is changed. Enabling this parameter will regenerate broken contact id's based on current configurations.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.39. Set latency_event_min_us parameter
configuration_examples.description: Defines a minimal pinging latency threshold, in microseconds, past which contact pinging latency update events will get raised. By default, an event is raised for each ping reply (i.e. latency update).
configuration_examples.code:
...
# raise an event for any 425+ ms pinging latency
modparam("usrloc", "latency_event_min_us", 425000)
...
configuration_examples.explanation: If both latency_event_min_us and latency_event_min_us_delta are set, the event will get raised if either of them is true.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.40. Set latency_event_min_us_delta parameter
configuration_examples.description: Defines a minimal, absolute pinging latency difference, in microseconds, past which contact pinging latency update events will get raised. The difference is computed using the latencies of the last two contact pinging replies. By default, an event is raised for each ping reply (i.e. latency update).
configuration_examples.code:
...
# raise an event only if a contact has pinging latency swings of 300+ ms
modparam("usrloc", "latency_event_min_us_delta", 300000)
...
configuration_examples.explanation: If both latency_event_min_us and latency_event_min_us_delta are set, the event will get raised if either of them is true.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.41. Set pinging_mode parameter
configuration_examples.description: Depending on the cluster_mode, the module can perform contact pinging using one of two possible heuristics: "ownership" or "cooperation".
configuration_examples.code:
...
# prepare an active/backup "full-sharing" setup, with no front-end
modparam("usrloc", "pinging_mode", "ownership")
...
configuration_examples.explanation: Notice that only the "full-sharing" clustering mode allows some flexibility -- all other modes are logically tied to a single pinging logic.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.42. Set mi_dump_kv_store parameter
configuration_examples.description: Enable in order to include the "KV-Store" field in all usrloc MI commands which output AoR or Contact representations. This verbose field contains custom data attached to each of these two entities.
configuration_examples.code:
...
# include the "KV-Store" key in all usrloc MI output
modparam("usrloc", "mi_dump_kv_store", 1)
...

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.43. Set contact_refresh_timer parameter
configuration_examples.description: Enable a timer which will periodically scan a sorted list of contacts and raise the E_UL_CONTACT_REFRESH for any of them which are past their re-registration time interval limit.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.44. ul_add_key usage
configuration_examples.description: Append a Key/Value to the Key-Value-Store of a Usrloc-Record.
configuration_examples.explanation: Returns false, if no record is found is usrloc.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.45. ul_get_key usage
configuration_examples.description: Retrieve a Key/Value from the Key-Value-Store of a Usrloc-Record.
configuration_examples.explanation: Returns false, if no record is found is usrloc or no according key is found.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.46. ul_del_key usage
configuration_examples.description: Deletes a Key/Value from the Key-Value-Store of a Usrloc-Record.
configuration_examples.explanation: Returns false, if no record is found is usrloc.
